app.U3RyaXBl.short_desc.message: Take payments and manage customers, invoices and payouts in Stripe

app.U3RyaXBl.desc.source:
Provides access to [Stripe](https://stripe.com), the payments platform, for taking money and managing everything around it.

**Common use cases**:
- **Payments**: start a payment, refund it in full or in part, and look up what was charged and what it cost
- **Customers**: create and update customers, attach payment sources to them, and credit or debit their balance
- **Billing**: raise invoices and subscribe customers to recurring prices
- **Reconciliation**: read the balance and the transactions behind each payout, so a deposit can be matched against the payments that made it up
- **Connect**: onboard connected accounts, add their payout destinations and the people on their legal entity, and act on their behalf

Authentication is a Stripe secret or restricted key, or an access token from Stripe Connect's OAuth2 flow. A **restricted key**, limited to the resources the integration needs, is the better choice in production.

Stripe is a trademark of Stripe, Inc.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.dXBkYXRlLWNvbm5lY3Rl.source:
A card or bank account to attach to the account for receiving [payouts](/connect/bank-debit-card-payouts) (you won’t be able to use it for top-ups). You can provide either a token, like the ones returned by [Stripe.js](/js), or a dictionary, as documented in the `external_account` parameter for [bank account](/api#account_create_bank_account) creation.

By default, providing an external account sets it as the new default external account for its currency, and deletes the old default if one exists. To add additional external accounts without replacing the existing default for the currency, use the [bank account](/api#account_create_bank_account) or [card creation](/api#account_create_card) APIs. After you create an [Account Link](/api/account_links) or [Account Session](/api/account_sessions), this property can only be updated for accounts where [controller.requirement_collection](/api/accounts/object#account_object-controller-requirement_collection) is `application`, which includes Custom accounts.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3JlYXRlLWFjY291bnQt.source:
Creates a single-use URL that sends a connected account holder into Stripe's hosted onboarding, where they enter the identity and bank details Stripe requires.

The link **expires a few minutes after it is created** and can only be used once, so create it at the moment the user is ready to be redirected rather than storing it. `refresh_url` is where Stripe sends them if it has expired, and `return_url` is where they land when they are done.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3JlYXRlLWFjY291bnQt.source:
The type of account link the user is requesting.

You can create Account Links of type `account_update` only for connected accounts where your platform is responsible for collecting requirements, including Custom accounts. You can't create them for accounts that have access to a Stripe-hosted Dashboard. If you use [Connect embedded components](/connect/get-started-connect-embedded-components), you can include components that allow your connected accounts to update their own information. For an account without Stripe-hosted Dashboard access where Stripe is liable for negative balances, you must use embedded components.

Creates an invoice for a customer.

A new invoice is a **draft**: it is not sent and cannot be paid until it is finalized, and while it is a draft its line items can still be changed. `automatically_finalizes_at` schedules that step. With `collection_method` set to `send_invoice` a `due_date` is required.

If [setup_future_usage](https://api.stripe.com#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Account after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Account instead.

If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.

When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](/strong-customer-authentication).

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y2hlY2tvdXQtc2Vzc2lv.message:
Fires when a customer finishes a Stripe Checkout session.

Completion means the customer got through the flow; check `payment_status` before fulfilling, because a session using a delayed payment method can complete while the payment is still pending.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItY3JlYXRl.source: React to a customer being created
app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItY3JlYXRl.message: React to a customer being created

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItY3JlYXRl.source:
Fires when a customer is created, however it happened - through the API, the dashboard, or a Checkout session.

Useful for keeping a CRM in step with Stripe without polling.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.aW52b2ljZS1jcmVhdGVk.message: React to an invoice being created

app.U3RyaXBl.action.aW52b2ljZS1jcmVhdGVk.source:
Fires when an invoice is created.

A new invoice is a **draft**, so this is the moment to add line items or a discount before it is finalized and sent.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.aW52b2ljZS1wYXltZW50.source: React to an invoice payment failing
app.U3RyaXBl.action.aW52b2ljZS1wYXltZW50.message: React to an invoice payment failing

app.U3RyaXBl.action.aW52b2ljZS1wYXltZW50.source:
Fires when payment of an invoice fails.

For a subscription this is the start of dunning, not the end of it: Stripe will retry on the account's schedule, so treat this as a prompt to ask the customer for a new payment method rather than as a cancellation.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.cGF5bWVudC1pbnRlbnQt.source:
Fires when a payment intent succeeds.

This is the reliable signal that a payment completed, including one that needed the customer to authenticate; it arrives whether or not the customer stayed on the page.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.cGF5bWVudC1pbnRlbnQt.source:
Fires when a payment intent fails.

`last_payment_error` says why. A failure is not always final - the same payment intent can be confirmed again with a different payment method.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.cGF5bWVudC1saW5rLWNy.source: React to a payment link being created
app.U3RyaXBl.action.cGF5bWVudC1saW5rLWNy.message: React to a payment link being created

app.U3RyaXBl.action.cGF5bWVudC1saW5rLWNy.source:
Fires when a payment link is created.

A payment link is a reusable URL that takes payments without any integration code, so this is useful for recording links colleagues create in the dashboard.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.source: React to a subscription being created
app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.message: React to a subscription being created

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.source:
Fires when a customer subscribes.

Check `status` before granting access: a subscription can start as `trialing`, or as `incomplete` when its first payment has not gone through yet.
app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.message:
Fires when a customer subscribes.

Check `status` before granting access: a subscription can start as `trialing`, or as `incomplete` when its first payment has not gone through yet.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.source:
Fires whenever a subscription changes - an upgrade or downgrade, a quantity change, a trial ending, or a payment failure moving it to `past_due`.

The event's `data.previous_attributes` holds only the fields that changed, which is the reliable way to tell what actually happened.

app.U3RyaXBl.action.Y3VzdG9tZXItc3Vic2Ny.source:
Fires when a subscription ends and billing stops.

This is the signal to revoke access. A subscription set to cancel at the end of its period stays active until then, and this fires when that moment arrives - not when the cancellation was requested.
